requirements.article: SR 11-7, Section III (Overview of Model Risk Management)
requirements.text: The institution applies a model definition covering any quantitative method, system or approach that applies statistical, economic, financial or mathematical theories, techniques and assumptions to process input data into quantitative estimates.
requirements.quote: a quantitative method, system, or approach that applies statistical, economic, financial, or mathematical theories, techniques, and assumptions to process input data into quantitative estimates
requirements.level_reason: Obligation concerning the institution's model risk management framework; evidenced in the MRM policy, not in model documentation.
requirements.verification_note: SR 11-7 (4 Apr 2011) attachment; rescinded 17 Apr 2026 and replaced by SR 26-2 / OCC Bulletin 2026-13, kept as industry reference. Same definition adopted in PRA SS1/23 Principle 1.1(a).

requirements.article: SR 11-7, Section III (Overview of Model Risk Management)
requirements.text: Model risk is managed like other types of risk: the institution identifies its sources and assesses its magnitude, for individual models and in aggregate.
requirements.quote: Model risk should be managed like other types of risk.
requirements.level_reason: Obligation concerning the institution's management of model risk in aggregate; evidenced in the MRM framework and aggregate model risk reporting, not in model documentation.
requirements.verification_note: SR 11-7 (4 Apr 2011) attachment; rescinded 17 Apr 2026 and replaced by SR 26-2 / OCC Bulletin 2026-13, kept as industry reference.

requirements.article: SR 11-7, Section III (Overview of Model Risk Management)
requirements.text: Model risk management is guided by effective challenge, performed by objective, informed parties with the competence, influence and incentives to identify model limitations and assumptions and produce appropriate changes.
requirements.quote: critical analysis by objective, informed parties who can identify model limitations and assumptions and produce appropriate changes
requirements.level_reason: Framework-level principle of the institution's model risk management; evidenced in the MRM policy and governance arrangements, not in model documentation.
requirements.verification_note: SR 11-7 (4 Apr 2011) attachment; rescinded 17 Apr 2026 and replaced by SR 26-2 / OCC Bulletin 2026-13, kept as industry reference.

requirements.article: SR 11-7, Section IV (Model Development, Implementation, and Use)
requirements.text: Data used to develop the model are rigorously assessed for quality and relevance, and any data proxies or adjustments are justified and documented.
requirements.verification_note: SR 11-7 (4 Apr 2011) attachment; rescinded 17 Apr 2026 and replaced by SR 26-2 / OCC Bulletin 2026-13, kept as industry reference.

requirements.article: SR 11-7, Section IV (Model Development, Implementation, and Use)
requirements.text: Model development starts from a clear statement of purpose, and the design, theory and logic are documented and supported by published research and sound industry practice.
requirements.verification_note: SR 11-7 (4 Apr 2011) attachment; rescinded 17 Apr 2026 and replaced by SR 26-2 / OCC Bulletin 2026-13, kept as industry reference.

requirements.article: SR 11-7, Section IV (Model Development, Implementation, and Use)
requirements.text: Model developers test the accuracy, robustness and stability of the model, assess its limitations and behaviour over a range of input values, and document the testing.
requirements.verification_note: SR 11-7 (4 Apr 2011) attachment; rescinded 17 Apr 2026 and replaced by SR 26-2 / OCC Bulletin 2026-13, kept as industry reference.

requirements.article: SR 11-7, Section IV (Model Development, Implementation, and Use)
requirements.text: Model users account for model uncertainty and limitations, for example through conservative adjustments or buffers, and understand the model's limitations when relying on its output.
requirements.verification_note: SR 11-7 (4 Apr 2011) attachment; rescinded 17 Apr 2026 and replaced by SR 26-2 / OCC Bulletin 2026-13, kept as industry reference.

requirements.text: Model validation is performed by staff independent of model development and use, with the requisite knowledge, skills, expertise and authority to challenge.
requirements.quote: Validation involves a degree of independence from model development and use.
requirements.level_reason: Obligation concerning the organisation and staffing of the validation function; evidenced in its organisational documentation, not in model documentation.
requirements.verification_note: SR 11-7 (4 Apr 2011) attachment; rescinded 17 Apr 2026 and replaced by SR 26-2 / OCC Bulletin 2026-13, kept as industry reference.

requirements.text: Validation evaluates the conceptual soundness of the model, including the quality of design and construction, the documentation, and the empirical evidence supporting methods and variable selection.
requirements.verification_note: SR 11-7 (4 Apr 2011) attachment; rescinded 17 Apr 2026 and replaced by SR 26-2 / OCC Bulletin 2026-13, kept as industry reference. First of the three core validation elements.

requirements.text: Ongoing monitoring, including process verification and benchmarking, confirms that the model is appropriately implemented and performs as intended as products, exposures and market conditions change.
requirements.verification_note: SR 11-7 (4 Apr 2011) attachment; rescinded 17 Apr 2026 and replaced by SR 26-2 / OCC Bulletin 2026-13, kept as industry reference. Second core validation element.

requirements.text: Outcomes analysis, including back-testing, compares model outputs with actual outcomes, with pre-defined thresholds for acceptable performance.
requirements.verification_note: SR 11-7 (4 Apr 2011) attachment; rescinded 17 Apr 2026 and replaced by SR 26-2 / OCC Bulletin 2026-13, kept as industry reference. Third core validation element.

requirements.text: Vendor and other third-party models are incorporated into the model risk management framework under the same principles as in-house models, with the institution validating its own use of the vendor product.
requirements.verification_note: SR 11-7 (4 Apr 2011) attachment; rescinded 17 Apr 2026 and replaced by SR 26-2 / OCC Bulletin 2026-13, kept as industry reference.

requirements.text: Each model is reviewed periodically, at least annually and more frequently if warranted, to determine whether it is working as intended and whether existing validation activities are sufficient.
requirements.verification_note: SR 11-7 (4 Apr 2011) attachment; rescinded 17 Apr 2026 and replaced by SR 26-2 / OCC Bulletin 2026-13, kept as industry reference.

requirements.article: SR 11-7, Section VI (Governance, Policies, and Controls)
requirements.text: The institution maintains a comprehensive firm-wide inventory of models in use, under development or recently retired.
requirements.level_reason: Obligation to maintain a firm-wide model inventory; evidenced in the model inventory, not in model documentation.
requirements.verification_note: SR 11-7 (4 Apr 2011) attachment; rescinded 17 Apr 2026 and replaced by SR 26-2 / OCC Bulletin 2026-13, kept as industry reference.

requirements.article: SR 11-7, Section VI (Governance, Policies, and Controls)
requirements.text: Model development and validation documentation is sufficiently detailed for parties unfamiliar with the model to understand how it operates, its limitations and its key assumptions.
requirements.verification_note: SR 11-7 (4 Apr 2011) attachment; rescinded 17 Apr 2026 and replaced by SR 26-2 / OCC Bulletin 2026-13, kept as industry reference.

requirements.article: SR 11-7, Section VI (Governance, Policies, and Controls)
requirements.text: Internal audit assesses the overall effectiveness of the model risk management framework, including whether validation is performed independently and effectively.
requirements.level_reason: Obligation of the internal audit function; evidenced in internal audit plans and reports, not in model documentation.
requirements.verification_note: SR 11-7 (4 Apr 2011) attachment; rescinded 17 Apr 2026 and replaced by SR 26-2 / OCC Bulletin 2026-13, kept as industry reference.
